o: Place n <= 18 numbers into numSlots <= 9 slots of capacity 2, maximizing sum of (number AND slot). Model slot occupancy as a bitmask of 2*numSlots bits where bit 2s and 2s+1 represent the two seats of slot s+1; the popcount of the mask equals how many numbers are placed, so processing numbers in a fixed order, dp(mask) = best AND-sum after placing popcount(mask) numbers. Transitions try every vacant seat. States 2^18 with 18 transitions each is about 5M operations — comfortably fast. Example 1 achieves 9 by pairing numbers with their own slot numbers where possible.
k: Encode both seats of every slot in one bitmask; popcount = numbers placed so far.
Memoized DFS over (index, mask) or bottom-up iteration over masks both work; nums[i] <= 15 keeps AND values tiny.

a.i: Recursively place the i-th number into any free seat; caching on (i, mask) collapses overlapping placements since the order of earlier placements only matters through the mask.
s: Define dp(i, mask): best sum placing nums[i..] given occupied seats.
For each slot s with a free seat, branch with value (nums[i] & (s+1)) + dp(i+1, mask | bit).
a.t: O(2^(2*S) * S) states-times-transitions with S = numSlots <= 9 — about 5M edge relaxations

a.i: Iterate masks in increasing order; since popcount(mask) equals the count of placed numbers, mask determines which number goes next — no recursion needed.
s: Allocate dp of size 2^(2S) initialized to 0.
For each mask with popcount i < n, push dp[mask] + (nums[i] & (s+1)) into every vacant seat's mask.
Answer is the max dp value over masks with popcount n (equivalently track a global max).
a.t: O(2^(2*S) * S) — each mask relaxed once per vacant seat

w: Either version passes; memoization uses less memory in practice (only reachable states), while bottom-up avoids recursion depth concerns. Pitfall: using numSlots bits instead of 2*numSlots — each slot holds TWO numbers. Empty slots are fine. Follow-up: capacity 3 per slot — triple the bits per slot, same technique.
